rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muʿaqqibāt are successive beings, each replacing the one before; most exegetes identify them here as guardian angels.
rows.anchor: المعقبات: المتناوبات التي يخلف كل واحد منها صاحبه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The muʿaqqibāt are angels of night who follow the angels of day.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء (¬6): المعقبات: ملائكة الليل تعقب ملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ uses ʿaqiba in the sense of ʿāqaba, like the paired forms ḍaʿufa/ḍāʿafa and ʿaqada/ʿāqada.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري (¬7): جعل الفراء عقب بمعنى عاقب، كما يقال: ضعف وضاعف

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: A muʿaqqib is one who returns to or follows up an action; the term also describes repeated raiding or returning to collect a debt.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم (¬8): كل من عمل عملا ثم عاد إليه وعقب

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Al-muʿaqqib is whatever follows what came before, and al-muʿaqqibāt are beings succeeding one another.
rows.anchor: وقال شمر (¬1): المعقب من كل شيء ما خلف يعقب ما قبله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The angels arrive one after another.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬2): المعقبات: ملائكة يأتي بعضهم بعقب بعض

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the form as a masculine plural of the feminine collective for angels; the masculine verb يحفظونه supports this.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء (¬3): والمعقبات ذكران جمع ملائكة معقبة ومعقبات

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the feminine form by the abundance of the angels, as with feminine forms used of a masculine person.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش (¬4): إنما أنث لكثرة ذلك منها نحو: نسابة وعلامة، وهو ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، والحسن، ومجاهد، وقتادة
rows.claim: They identify the muʿaqqibāt as guardian angels, supported by the report that angels of night and day alternate and meet at dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬5): وسعيد بن جبير (¬6)

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A prophetic report says angels of night and day take turns among people and meet at the dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: يتعاقب فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of the angels also explains the dawn recitation as witnessed: night angels ascend while day angels descend.
rows.anchor: قيل تصعد ملائكة الليل وتنزل ملائكة النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in له may refer to من in من أسر, which is general, or alternatively to God in the phrase about the unseen and the seen.
rows.anchor: والكناية في قوله (له) تعود على (من) في (من أسر) وهو واقع على العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the angel interpretation, God has guardian angels who successively descend to earth in front of and behind a person.
rows.anchor: لله ملائكة حفظة تتعاقب في النزول إلى الأرض من بين يدي الإنسان ومن خلفه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: One reading places من أمر الله before the verb: the person has angels from God's command who guard him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنه على التقديم والتأخير، تقديره: له معقبات من أمر الله يحفظونه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Saʿīd's transmission, the angels are from God's command.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قول ابن عباس (¬2) في رواية سعيد في هذه الآية، قال: هم الملائكة، وهم من أمر الله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: A second reading supplies an omitted noun: the protection itself is from what God has commanded.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أن هذا على إضمار، أي: ذلك الحفظ من أمر الله

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains the ellipsis as omission of the noun while retaining its predicate, like saying that what is in a purse is two thousand.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري فحذف الاسم وأبقى خبره

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj likewise takes the phrase to mean that their guarding the person is by God's command.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الزجاج (¬3)؛ لأنه قال: المعنى: حفظهم إياه من أمر الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: A third reading gives من the sense of باء, so the angels guard him by God's command; the author accepts all these readings.
rows.anchor: والتأويل يحفظونه بأمر الله، وقد صحت هذه الأقوال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿIkrima's transmission, the angels guard a person in front and behind, but leave him when the decree comes.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة (¬1): يحفظونه من بين يديه ومن خلفه، فإذا جاء القدر خلوا بينه وبينه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Every person has an assigned angel who wards off jinn, humans, and vermin, saying they must stay away, unless God permits harm.
rows.anchor: روى ليث عن مجاهد (¬2) قال: ما من عبد إلا به ملك موكل بحفظه من الجن والإنس والهوام

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Angels defend people from the evil of jinn and vermin; without them the jinn would snatch people away.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب (¬3): لولا أن الله -عز وجل- وكل بكم ملائكة يذبون عنكم لتخطفتكم الجن

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets يحفظونه as keeping account for the person of good and bad deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج (¬4): معنى (يحفظونه) يحفظون عليه، أي: يحفظون عليه الحسنات

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd glosses the record as preserving the person's speech and actions.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد (¬6): يعني: يحفظون عليه قوله وفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not take a people's blessing away until they commit sins.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يسلب قوما نعمة حتى يعملوا بمعاصيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates the verse to the grounds between God and creation and applies it to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): يريد العذر فيما بينه وبين خلقه، ويعني بهذا أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage links this change of blessing with those who exchanged God's blessing for disbelief and brought their people to ruin.
rows.anchor: كما قال: {ألم تر إلى الذين بدلوا نعمت الله كفرا وأحلوا قومهم دار البوار}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Here سوء means punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): يريد عذابا

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: When God wills punishment, the guardian angels cannot avert it.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك عن ابن عباس (¬3): لم تغن المعقبات شيئا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: No one can repel God's punishment or overturn His decree.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه (¬4): لا راد لعذابي ولا ناقض لحكمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wālin is one who takes charge of the people and shields them from punishment.
rows.anchor: يلي أمرهم ويمنع العذاب عنهم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The relative pronoun الذين is accusative, appositional to من; the sense is that God guides those who believe.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬6): (الذين) في موضع نصب ردا على (من)، المعنى: يهدي الله الذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When believers hear the Quran their hearts humble and settle; when they hear God's remembrance they love it and find comfort in it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬7): يريد إذا سمعوا القرآن خشعت قلوبهم واطمأنت

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil gives a similar explanation of believers' hearts settling through remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال # مقاتل (¬1)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: When they remember God alone, believers affirm Him without doubt, unlike those who recoil at God's sole mention because they deny the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي إذا ذكروا الله وحده آمنوا به غير شاكين، بخلاف من وصف بقوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: The hearts that find tranquility through God's remembrance are the hearts of believers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) وغيره: يريد قلوب المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says a disbeliever's heart is not tranquil; he reconciles this verse with the believers' hearts trembling at God's mention in al-Anfāl.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬4): لأن الكافر غير مطمئن القلب

rows.speaker: الحسن وغيره
rows.claim: God sent Muhammad to his community just as He sent prophets to earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن (¬7) وغيره: أرسلناك كما أرسلنا الأنبياء قبلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The community is a generation whose predecessors were earlier generations.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬8): في قرن قد خلت من قبلها قرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation Muhammad recites to them is the Quran.
rows.anchor: {لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك} يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed after Abū Jahl heard Muhammad invoke al-Raḥmān at al-Ḥijr and accused him before the polytheists of invoking two gods.
rows.anchor: كان في # الحجر يدعو، وأبو جهل يسمع إليه، وهو يقول: يا رحمن

rows.speaker: مقاتل، وابن جريج، وقتادة
rows.claim: They say the passage about calling God al-Raḥmān was revealed at the Ḥudaybiyya treaty when the polytheists objected to writing the basmala and asked for باسمك اللهم.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬2) وابن جريج (¬3) وقتادة (¬4): نزل هذا في صلح الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to tell the deniers that al-Raḥmān, whose identity they rejected, is his Lord and master, with no deity but Him.
rows.anchor: إن الرحمن الذي أنكرتم معرفته، هو إلهي وسيدي، لا إله إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent with proofs of his prophethood, including the hand and staff and other signs.
rows.anchor: أي: بالبراهين التي دلت على صحة نبوته مثل اليد والعصا وغيرهما من آيات موسى

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The particle أن in أن أخرج may be a lightened declarative particle or an explanatory particle meaning أي.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أن) هاهنا يصلح أن تكون المخففة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: On the explanatory reading, God sent Moses with signs and told him to lead his people out, like the chiefs' command in Ṣād to go away.
rows.anchor: ولكون المعنى: {ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا} أي (¬4): أخرج قومك

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: On the lightened declarative reading, God sent Moses to lead his people out; the preposition is omitted and أن connects to an imperative form with declarative sense.
rows.anchor: كان المعنى: أرسلناه بأن يخرج قومه، إلا أن الجار حذف ووصلت (أن) بلفظ الأمر

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh is cited for both grammatical analyses of أن.
rows.anchor: وحكي القولين عن سيبويه (¬7)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The movement from darkness into light means moving from associating partners with God to faith.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من الشرك إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A day runs from sunrise to sunset, and the plural أيام is historically formed from أيوام with one of the adjacent quiescent yāʾ and wāw assimilated.
rows.anchor: وكانت الأيام في الأصل: أيوام واجتمعت الياء والواو، سبقت إحداهما بالسكون

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Arabic uses days for events, blessings, and punishments because they occur during days.
rows.anchor: ويعبر بالأيام عن الوقائع والنعم والنقم؛ لأن هذه كلها تقع فيها، ذكره شمر

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: The Arabs use أيام for historical events: someone who knows the days of the Arabs knows their notable episodes.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: العرب تقول: الأيام في معنى الوقائع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: They interpret God's days as His blessings; Ubayy transmits this interpretation from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: يريد بنعم الله

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet explains God's days as His blessings, in a report transmitted by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: رواه عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في قوله: {وذكرهم بأيام الله}

rows.speaker: الحسن، وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr give an interpretation like the blessings reading.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الحسن (¬1)، وسعيد بن جبير (¬2)

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān interprets the days as God's episodes involving earlier nations.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل بن سليمان: بوقائع الله في الأمم السالفة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says to remind them of blessings and of punishments by which God avenged Noah, ʿĀd, and Thamūd.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرهم بنعم أيام الله عليهم، وبنقم أيام الله التي انتقم فيها من قوم نوح وعاد وثمود

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says to warn them with the punishments of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and others, and with God's pardoning of others, using severity and leniency.
rows.anchor: يقول: خوفهم بما نزل بعاد وثمود وغيرهم من العذاب، وبالعفو

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The command exhorts by promise and threat: recall blessings on past believers and God's vengeance on those who denied messengers, so people accept the promise and avoid denial.
rows.anchor: يقول: عظهم بالترغيب (والترهيب، والوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Days can mean alternating fortunes and episodes of good and evil; the text cites God's alternation of days among people and an Arabic proverb about seeing a day of joy and then a comparable day of loss.
rows.anchor: ومن الأيام التي أريد بها الدول من النعيم (¬3) قوله تعالى: {وتلك الأيام نداولها بين الناس}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A صبار is patient in obeying God and refraining from disobedience, while a شكور is grateful for God's blessings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لكل صبار على طاعة الله وعن معاصيه، شكور لأنعم الله

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The verse means every believer, since patience and gratitude are believers' acts and every situation is either blessing or hardship; the believer is grateful in one and patient in the other.
rows.anchor: أراد لآيات لكل مؤمن؛ لأن الصبر والشكر من أفعال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God has chosen some servants for Himself and tells Iblīs of that special choosing; Iblīs has no power or argument to lead them to shirk and error.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: استأثر الله عبادا واصطنعهم لنفسه، فأخبر إبليس باصطناعه إياهم

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna identifies these servants as the chosen ones whom God guided and selected.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: هؤلاء ثنية (¬4) الذين هداهم # واجتباهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says they are those whom Iblīs himself excepted from his threat.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هؤلاء هم الذين استثنى إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of the overturning and stone rain is given in the commentary on Hūd, verse 82.
rows.anchor: مفسر في سورة هود [آية: 82]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of توسم is to see a trace of good in someone or discern good in them by observation.
rows.anchor: يقال: توسمت في فلان خيرا، إذا رأيت فيه أثرا منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, المتوسمين means people with discernment; Mujāhid, al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, and Ibn Qutayba agree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: للمتفرسين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the term as onlookers.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: للناظرين

rows.speaker: مقاتل وابن زيد
rows.claim: Muqātil and Ibn Zayd interpret the term as reflective people.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل وابن زيد: للمتفكرين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the term as people who take a lesson.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: للمعتبرين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses the term as perceptive observers and cites a line by Zuhayr using المتوسم of an observant viewer.
rows.anchor: أنشد لزهير: وفيهن ملهى للطيف ومنظر ... أنيق لعين الناظر المتوسم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: In its precise lexical sense, a mutawassim scrutinizes a mark until its true signification is known; one recognizes a quality in someone by looking.
rows.anchor: وحقيقته في اللغة؛ المتوسمون النظار المتثبتون في نظرهم حتى يعرفوا حقيقة سمة الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaṣd means straightness: a straight path leads a person to the intended destination.
rows.anchor: القصد: استقامة الطريق، يقال: طريق قصد وقاصد إذا أداك إلى مطلوبك

rows.speaker: جابر، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن عباس
rows.claim: Most exegetes, including these authorities, understand that God explains the straight path through books, messengers, and proofs; al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj choose this reading.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن المعنى: وعلى الله بيان قصد السبيل بالكتب والرسل والحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This first interpretation supplies an omitted annex: the verse means that explaining the straight path is God's responsibility.
rows.anchor: الآية من باب حذف المضاف؛ لأن التقدير: وعلى الله بيان قصد السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāʾir means deviating from the right, and منها refers to the feminine السبيل: some paths deviate from the truth.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الجور في اللغة: الميل عن الحق (¬5)، والكناية في منها تعود على السبيل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the deviating paths as Judaism, Christianity, and Magianism.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: يعني اليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak identifies the deviating paths as whims and innovations.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المبارك: يعني الأهواء والبدع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, God makes faith's path easy for whom He guides and difficult for whom He misleads; this is illustrated by the hypocrite and disbeliever burdened by purification and Ramadan fasting.
rows.anchor: روى عطاء عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية، قال: من أراد أن يهديه سهل له طريق الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse affirms that guidance is God's choice: had He willed, He would have guided everyone so that no one differed from Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يريد: فلو شاء لأرشدكم أجمعين حتى لا يختلف عليك يا محمد أحد

rows.speaker: مجاهد، وعبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: An alternative reading says the straight path, namely Ḥanīfism and Islam, leads to God's pleasure, reward, and recompense; Mujāhid and Ibn al-Mubārak hold it.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب مجاهد، قال: على الله طريق الحق (¬2)، وبه قال عبد الله بن المبارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers this second interpretation because it needs no ellipsis and raises no Qadari objection; the first might seem to attribute the straight path to God in the contested sense.
rows.anchor: وهو أقوى القولين؛ لأنه صح من غير إضمار ولا شبهة للقدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative interpretation is linked to God's statement that the straight path is upon Him, meaning it leads to His reward and honor.
rows.anchor: كقوله: {قال هذا صراط علي مستقيم} [الحجر: 41]، أي: أنه يؤدي إلى جزائي وكرامتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word علامات is coordinated with what precedes it; a sign is a perceptible form conveying meaning, and its root is علم.
rows.anchor: وعلامات} منسوقة (¬3) على ما قبلها، والعلامة صورة يعلم بها المعنى

rows.speaker: الكلبي والقرظي
rows.claim: They identify the signs as mountains, landmarks by day like the stars at night; on this reading the clause ends here, as al-Akhfash holds.
rows.anchor: فقال الكلبي والقرظي: يعني الجبال (¬4)، وهي علامات للطرق بالنهار كالنجوم بالليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, the signs are the stars in the sky, but the author prefers mountains because the signs are coordinated with things created on earth and the verse then distinguishes the star.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية # عطاء: يريد نجوم السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that if علامات meant stars the wording would say by them; the following mention of the star shows that the signs are something other than stars.
rows.anchor: فلما قال: {وبالنجم} دل أن المراد بالعلامات غير النجم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وإبراهيم
rows.claim: They interpret guidance by the star as guidance by all stars; al-Zajjāj chooses this, since singular نجم can have the same collective sense as its plural.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وإبراهيم: أراد جميع النجوم (¬3)، واختاره الزجاج

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, the star means the constellation al-Jady.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يعني الجدي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the stars as al-Thurayyā and Banāt Naʿsh.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني الثريا وبنات نعش

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies them as the two Firqads and al-Jady; al-Farrāʾ chooses this view.
rows.anchor: يعني الفرقدين والجدي (¬1)، وهو اختيار الفراء (¬2)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars guide people to roads and the direction of prayer on land and sea.
rows.anchor: أي إلى الطريق والقبلة في البر والبحر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وجميع المفسرين
rows.claim: Here الدين means obedience and واصب means lasting; the verb وصب denotes continuing.
rows.anchor: الدين: الطاعة هاهنا، والواصب: الدائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lasting quality is illustrated by the Quran's phrase عذاب واصب and by the verb واظب for persisting in something.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {ولهم عذاب واصب} [الصافات: 9] ويقال: واظب على الشيء وواصب عليه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says obedience to God is eternally obligatory.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي طاعته واجبة أبدا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
rows.claim: Every other being's obedience ends through disappearance or death, whereas obedience to God endures.
rows.anchor: ليس من أحد يدان له ويطاوع إلا انقطع ذلك عنه بزوال أو هلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing question asks whether people fear anyone besides God, who has shown that He alone is one and creator of everything and forbids associating another deity with Him.
rows.anchor: أفغير الله الذي قد أبان لكم أنه واحد، وأنه خالق كل شيء، وأمر أن لا يتخذ معه إله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥā and awḥā are equivalent; here God's revelation to the bee is inspiration placed within it.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وأوحى ربك} الآية. وحى وأوحى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bee is the honey-making wasp, and its singular is naḥla.
rows.anchor: النحل: زنبور (¬5) العسل، والواحدة نحلة (¬6)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj suggests the bee is named for being a gift from which God gives people honey.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: جائز أن يكون سمي نحلا؛ لأن الله عز وجل نحل الناس العسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says النحل can be masculine or feminine; it is feminine in Hijaz Arabic, as in the verse, and plurals marked only by a feminine ending are feminine.
rows.anchor: النحل يذكر ويؤنث (¬1)، وهي مؤنثة في لغة الحجاز

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: God inspires every living creature to seek benefits and avoid harms; the bee is singled out as a striking lesson in subtle design, including its inspired construction of homes.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى أوحى إلى كل دابة وذي روح وحي الإلهام في التماس منافعها واجتناب مضارها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Bees make homes for themselves in mountains when those places have no human owners.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي تتخذ من الجبال لأنفسها إذا كانت لا أصحاب لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ومما يعرشون means what people build and roof; the verb was read with either a u-vowel or an i-vowel on the rāʾ, like two forms of يعكف.
rows.anchor: أي: يبنون ويسقفون، وفيه لغتان: قرئ بها ضم الراء (¬4) وكسرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās understands it as hives that people build for bees.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ما يعرش الناس لها من الجباح (¬6)؛ وهو: خلايا # النحل (¬1)

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets what people trellis as grapevines, but the author rejects this here because bees do not inhabit vines; the intended construction is their hives.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد في قوله: {ومما يعرشون} هو الكروم (¬2)، ولا معنى للكروم هاهنا

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Without God's subjection and inspiration, bees would not live in the houses people build for them.
rows.anchor: لولا التسخير وإلهام الله تعالى ما كانت تأوي إلى ما يبني لها الناس من بيوتها

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: The command to eat from all fruits is not universal in scope, as in the Quran's statements that the Queen was given everything and that the wind destroyed everything.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: أي من الثمرات، وكل هاهنا لا يقع على العموم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The bee follows its Lord's paths by seeking pasture along them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد طرق ربك (¬5)، تطلب فيها الرعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhululan is the plural of dhalūl, meaning yielding, gentle, or subdued; it is also said of a compliant horse.
rows.anchor: يقال: فرس ذلول بين الذل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says no place the bee travels becomes rough or difficult for it; on this reading dhululan describes the paths.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لا يتوعر عليها مكان سلكته (¬2)، فعلى هذا الذلل من صفة السبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds it more apt that God has made the bee's routes easy, an interpretation chosen by al-Zajjāj.
rows.anchor: الأشبه: لا تتوعر عليها لتذليل الله لها إياها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda takes dhululan to mean obedient; Ibn Qutayba chooses this because the bees are subdued by God's control.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذللا يعني مطيعة (¬5)، وهو اختيار ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records both analyses: dhululan can describe the paths or the bees, which are subdued so that the drink issues from their bellies.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء القولين، فقال: ذللا نعت للسبيل، ويقال: نعت للنحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammar shifts from addressing the bee directly to reporting about it.
rows.anchor: رجوع من الخطاب إلى الخبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The drink's colors include red, white, and yellow.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: منه أحمر وأبيض وأصفر

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The bee eats sour, bitter, and otherwise unpalatable things, which God transforms into honey; it expels honey from its mouth like human saliva.
rows.anchor: هي تأكل الحامض والمر وما لا يوصف طعمه فيحيل الله ذلك عسلا

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the pronoun in فيه back to the drink, honey, and say it contains healing for people.
rows.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن الكناية تعود إلى قوله: {شراب}، وهو العسل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj answers the objection that honey can harm some people by analogy with water: it sustains life but can kill someone whose illness makes it harmful.
rows.anchor: أجاب عن هذا الزجاج، وقال: الماء حياة كل شيء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says honey heals the illnesses for which it is a remedy.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قول السدي: فيه شفاء للأوجاع التي شفاؤها فيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the healing as being in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد: {فيه شفاء للناس}: أي في القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the Quranic account of the bee and other stories is healing because it proves God's oneness, explains lawful and unlawful matters, and removes doubts; this accords with the Quran being healing for hearts.
rows.anchor: فيما قصصنا عليكم من قصة النحل في القرآن وسائر القصص التي تدل على أن الله واحد، شفاء للناس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says honey cures every disease while the Quran heals what is in people's hearts.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: العسل فيه شفاء من كل داء، والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj transmit both the honey and Quran interpretations of healing.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفراء والزجاج القولين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some prefer the honey interpretation as closer to the apparent wording and cite Abū Saʿīd's report: the Prophet twice told a man to give honey to his sick brother, then said God spoke truth and the brother's belly lied; the brother recovered.
rows.anchor: واختار قوم القول الأول؛ وقالوا: إنه أليق بظاهر الكتاب

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In a report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, the Prophet prescribes honey for the man's brother's stomach illness and says God spoke truth when the repeated dose cures him; the author gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فقال: إن أخي تشتكي بطنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The sign in the bee's story points to God's greatness and power.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في عظمة الله وقدرته

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash reads الرحمن as an explanatory statement: He is the All-Merciful.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: (هو الرحمن)

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad parses الرحمن as the predicate of an omitted subject: after the mention of the One who created, the sense is He is the All-Merciful.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: ({الرحمن} مرفوع على خبر المبتدأ المضمر)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted subject in al-Mubarrad's parsing is illustrated by the phrase ففي النار, meaning in the Fire.
rows.anchor: المعنى ففي النار

rows.speaker: كثير من أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Many exegetes interpret استوى as استولى, meaning took possession or prevailed.
rows.anchor: قال كثير من أهل التأويل: استوى معناه استولى

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā was asked about the verse and said istiwāʾ means turning toward something.
rows.anchor: قال: (سئل أحمد بن يحيى عن قول الله تعالى: {الرحمن على العرش استوى} فقال: الاستواء الإقبال على الشيء)

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash, like Abū ʿUbayda, interprets استوى as ascending or rising above, as in the idiom of mounting an animal or roof.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: (استوى أي علا تقول: استويت فوق الدابة وعلى ظهر البيت أي علوته)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the rising interpretation, God is above the Throne by His power and might; the Throne is singled out because it is the greatest creation.
rows.anchor: أنه عز وجل علا على العرش بقدرته وقوته، وخص العرش بالذكر؛ لأنه أعظم المخلوقات

rows.speaker: مالك، والشافعي، والأوزاعي، والثوري
rows.claim: The leading early authorities named here avoided discussion of this verse and similar verses; the author calls that their way.
rows.anchor: وعامة السلف أعرضوا عن الكلام في هذه الآية ونظائرها وذلك طريقة مالك، والشافعي، والأوزاعي، والثوري

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad permits Allah to be the subject with لا إله إلا هو as predicate, or a predicate of the omitted subject هو, meaning He is God.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: يجوز أن يكون {الله} ابتداء، وخبره {لا إله إلا هو}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration means no object of worship deserves worship except God.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: لا معبود يستحق العبادة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beautiful names are the ninety-nine names transmitted in a report.
rows.anchor: {له الأسماء الحسنى} يعني: التسعة والتسعين التي ورد بها الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine of al-aḥsan; one feminine adjective can describe a plural as a collective unity, as in the cited Quranic examples.
rows.anchor: والحسنى تأنيث الأحسن، كالكبرى والعليا، ووحدت الحسنى والأسماء جمع

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq infers that Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh and addressed him as God had reported, since Pharaoh then asks Moses who their Lord is.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (المعنى فأتياه فقالا له ما أخبر الله في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that Pharaoh asks Moses about both Moses' and Aaron's Lord, but uses the singular address because Moses alone is being addressed.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن المعنى فمن ربك وربه يا موسى، فغلب الخطاب؛ لأن المخاطب كان موسى دون هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading addresses both brothers while omitting Aaron's name to suffice with Moses and to match the verse endings.
rows.anchor: [الثاني: أن كليهما مخاطب، ترك ذكر هارون]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular قال ربنا supports that Moses alone answered; if both brothers were addressed, they would have answered together.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أن المخاطب موسى دون هارون قوله تعالى: {قال ربنا} ولم يقل: قالا
